experimental_design: Four PDA lawn plates were made using isolate JB5. Lawn plates were inoculated 10/9/2024; incubated for 120 hours between 10/9/2024 and 10/14/2024; sliced into small chunks and frozen in two 50mL conical tubes 10/14/2024 (two plates of agar per tube); then thawed 10/16/2024. Following thaw, agar chunks were soaked in 3:1 ethyl acetate:water solution and centrifuged to move the extracted inhibitory chemical(s) to the ethyl acetate while the primary metabolites remained in the water. Ethyl acetate containing extracted inhibitory chemical(s) were removed from conical tubes using Pasteur pipets, combined in a beaker, dried with sodium sulfate, and then gravity filtered to produce the final solution ideally containing only ethyl acetate and the extracted inhibitory chemical.

Finally, after letting the solution settle, we transferred the top solution off (ethyl acetate layer) and pipetted it into a clean beaker, added some drying solvent (sodium sulfate) to absorb the remaining water in the ethyl acetate layer, and then gravity filtered it into a clean vial. It is now sitting in a fume hood so that the ethyl acetate evaporates.

The agar is then mixed with ethyl acetate and water, allowing the antibacterial chemicals to partition into the ethyl acetate layer. After mixing and centrifuging the mixture to separate the layers, the ethyl acetate layer is collected. Finally, the ethyl acetate is evaporated, leaving behind a dried residue of the extracted antibacterial chemicals.

experimental_design:
Tiny Earth Chemical Extraction of Antibiotics 
 In preparation for chemical extraction of antibiotics, Ab+ isolate AB5 was used to create a lawn on PDA using a sterile swab to spread a colony from Ab+ library. The plate was then incubated at 28°C for 7 days. Afterwards the plate was chopped up using a cutting device, transferred into a labeled flask, capped and placed into a dry ice bath/ethanol bath for 20-30 minutes. Underneath a fume hood, 15-mL of ethyl acetate was then added to the flask using a 10-mL serological pipette and pump. The flask was capped and placed on a shaker at room temperature for 48 hours. After shaking, with a 10-mL serological pipette all liquid, ideally 15-mL, is transferred into a scintillation vial and left uncapped to dry for 7 days. Dried-down extract in vials were then resuspened by pipetting 250-µL of methanol into the vials.

experimental_design: We obtained a sample of isolate A2 on a sterile swab and created a lawn on a 50% TSBA plate. The plate was incubated for 168 hours (one week) at 28C, then cut up with a sterile device into small enough pieces that would fit into a 250mL flask. The flask was covered with tin foil and labeled, then flash frozen for 20 minutes. After the flash freezing, we used Pasteur pipettes to add 15mL of ethyl acetate into the flask, then we re-covered the flask and put it onto a shaker at room temperature (25C) for 48 hours. After the incubation period, the chemical extract was pipetted out and placed into a small vial. This vial was parafilmed and covered with tin foil then labeled. The vial was left to dry for 168 hours (one week) and resuspended with 250uL of methanol to be used for eukaryotic and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

experimental_design:
1. Create a dense lawn of isolate using a sterile swab on the agar media it's been cultured on throughout the semester. 
 2. Incubate at 28C for 186 hours. 
 3. Using a scoopula or spatula, chop up the agar plate into 1.0 cm diameter squares and transfer to an Erlenmeyer flask. 
 4. Place flask in a dry ice bath for 20 minutes. 
 5. Remove flask and aliquot 10 ml of ethyl acetate into the flask. 
 6. Cover with aluminum foil and place on shaker at room temperature until next lab period (48-120 hours). 
 7. Remove from shaker and transfer all liquid (~ 10 mL) into a labeled scintillation vial. 
 8. Leave uncapped in fume hood until liquid is completely dry and only extract remains. 
 9. Resuspend solid extract in 250 uL methanol.
